raw_response:
This is my plan for this year. I have farmed 20 years in Quzhou, I know this land.

I split my 10.1 mu like this: 3 mu for cotton on the sandy corner where wheat does not do so well, and 7.1 mu for the wheat-maize rotation on the better soil. This is how I did it last year and the year before — no reason to change since prices are not much different.

**Wheat (winter, 7.1 mu):** I plant improved variety, Jimai or Shimai seed from the town dealer, whichever is cheaper this season. Last year my neighbor Old Wang got 480 kg/mu with Jimai 22, so I keep to that. Before planting I spread 40 kg diammonium phosphate and 15 kg potassium sulfate per mu as base, then rotary till to mix it in. In spring at jointing I topdress about 15 kg urea per mu with the irrigation. Total nitrogen comes to around 17 kg/mu. I water 3 times — once before winter (dong shui), once at jointing in March, once at grain filling. I spray 2 times, one for aphids and one combined spray for powdery mildew and wheat midge at heading.

**Maize (summer, 7.1 mu):** After wheat harvest in June I direct-seed hybrid maize — Zhengdan 958 or similar — no tillage, straight into the stubble. I put about 40 kg compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu at planting, then side-dress 20 kg urea at the big bell stage. Nitrogen about 15 kg/mu total. I only irrigate once if July rain is not enough. One spray for corn borer and armyworm. Last year I got 550 kg/mu so that is my target.

**Cotton (spring, 3 mu):** I plant improved Bt cotton to save on bollworm sprays — this has been reliable for me. I plough deep before planting in late April. Base fertilizer I use is 25 kg diammonium phosphate, 10 kg potassium sulfate, plus 10 kg urea per mu. Then 2 topdressings of urea, about 8 kg each at squaring and flowering. Total nitrogen around 18 kg/mu. I water 2 times from the well, at squaring and peak flowering. Cotton still needs 4 sprays — aphids early, then mirid bugs and spider mites, even with Bt. I aim for 260 kg/mu seed cotton, that is what this land gives.

I always put a little more fertilizer than the agronomist says, because I cannot afford a bad harvest. Fertilizer is money, but losing grain is worse.
